n: Those who trust the Lord are as stable as Mount Zion itself — unshakable and enduring.

f.w: as mount Zion, which cannot be removed

n: Jerusalem is ringed by higher hills; just so, the Lord surrounds his people with protection forever.

f.w: the mountains are round about Jerusalem

n: The wicked’s ‘rod’ — their scepter or rule — will not stay over the land given to the righteous, so that the righteous aren’t pressured into evil.

f.g: The scepter — rule — of the wicked.
The land allotted to the righteous.

n: A prayer: Lord, do good to those who are good and honest-hearted.
Those who turn aside to crooked paths will be led away with evildoers. The psalm closes with a blessing: peace be upon Israel.
